cause: The raw-response observer classified a singleton with any valid user_id as present, even when it differed from the queried and signed-in owner.
repair: The initial-read caller passes its verified identity to the observer. The observer classifies a 200 GET response only when its single user_id equality filter requests that identity; a singleton must also carry the same user_id. Owner IDs remain private to the observer and are omitted from snapshots and reports.

red.before_repair: 16 passed, 2 failed: plain and base64 wrong-owner singleton cases returned true instead of null through the actual Supabase query and Network callback.

green.result: 40 passed, 0 failed. The actual initial-read gate accepts matching present and absent responses and refuses wrong-owner, wrong-filter, null, malformed, and multiple-row responses. The existing pre-write owner-read refusal tests remain green.

limits: No native browser run, live database read, build, or release in this narrow lane.
The historical raw response body was unavailable, so these controlled wire responses establish guard behavior rather than historical row state.
